children: Singapore upgraded its 2026 economic growth forecast to around 6.0% on Tuesday after posting third-quarter expansion of 6.1% from a year earlier, government data showed.
The July to September growth was higher than an official advance estimate of 5.4% and above the 5.6% expected in a Reuters poll of economists​.
On a quarter-on-quarter, seasonally adjusted basis, gross domestic product expanded by 1.5% in the July-September period, compared with an advance estimate of 1.1% growth.
The Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry now expects 2027 GDP growth to come in at a range of 2.5% to 4.5%.

"Although elevated energy prices have contributed to global inflationary pressures and tighter monetary policy in several economies, on balance, METI’s assessment is that Singapore’s external demand outlook for the year has improved compared to the assessment in August," the ministry said.
In a separate statement, Enterprise Singapore upgraded its non-oil domestic exports forecast to a growth of 30% to 32% in 2026, from 14% to 16% previously.
That was driven primarily by AI-related growth in electronics and specialised machinery as well as support from lumpy exports of the structures of ships and boats.

Singapore had in August upgraded its growth forecast for this year to 4.5% to 5.5%, from a previous range of 2.0% to 4.0%, saying the impact of the Middle East war had been less severe than initially feared while the global AI investment boom had been stronger than expected.
Singapore's key consumer price gauge rose 1.5% in October from a year earlier.
Last month, the central bank kept its monetary settings unchanged in a move that surprised analysts, with inflation risks expected to ease slightly as the AI boom and supply constraints moderate.
